biography: Mika Thomas, the 'Taco Tornado' as some have affectionately dubbed him (much to his chagrin), hails from the vibrant streets of Guadalajara, Mexico. Racing wasn't in his bloodline – his family ran a successful bakery – but the roar of engines always captivated him. At 12, he secretly saved up enough money from his part-time job to buy a battered go-kart. He'd sneak out to a makeshift track on the outskirts of town, honing his skills under the watchful eye of an old mechanic named Ricardo. His raw talent was undeniable. At 16, he entered a local karting championship and, against all odds, won. This caught the attention of a small, independent racing team. Now, at 18, Mika is making waves in the Formula 4 circuit, his flashy driving style and undeniable speed turning heads, even if his consistency is still a work in progress.
drivingStyle: Mika is an aggressive, all-or-nothing driver. He attacks corners with gusto, often flirting with the limits of grip. His tire management is, generously put, 'enthusiastic,' prioritizing outright pace over long-run conservation. Under pressure, Mika either crumbles spectacularly or elevates his game to another level – there's rarely an in-between. He thrives on the thrill of overtaking, often attempting audacious moves that leave spectators breathless (and his mechanics sweating).

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos during a junior karting event led to an on-track collision and a simmering rivalry ever since. Alessandro represents the established order, something Mika is determined to disrupt.
They've been neck and neck in the championship standings all season, with several close finishes and heated battles. The rivalry is respectful but fierce, fueled by a mutual desire to win.
Kenji and Mika had a particularly nasty incident during a practice session where Kenji accused Mika of blocking him intentionally. Mika has denied those claims, but the tension lingers.

quirks: Always wears a lucky wristband his grandmother knitted for him.
Listens to mariachi music at full volume right before the race to 'get pumped'.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, or I'm going home.
careerHighlight: Winning the Guadalajara Karting Championship in his first attempt, proving to everyone (including himself) that he had what it takes.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix, costing him a potential podium and severely damaging his confidence.
